title: After a wrong figure reached management, numbers are no longer trusted until cross-checked
body: A single incident, where the director asked about a gap she could not explain, changed the participant's behaviour: she now cross-checks every number herself before trusting it. This is stated explicitly and tied to a concrete event; it explains why the reporting is redone outside the tool. > "The director asked me where the gap came from and I had no answer. Since then, I don't trust the numbers until I've cross-checked them myself." > - Claire Martin, [[interview-claire-martin]] ## Connections - extends [[pulse-numbers-do-not-always-match-the-carriers-data]] - the data mismatch is the trigger for the loss of trust - explains [[the-weekly-management-report-is-rebuilt-by-hand-in-excel]] - cross-checking is done through the Excel rebuild

title: Ops leads need to be able to explain every number to management
body: The participant does not ask for perfect data; she asks for enough context to justify the figures she presents. Inference: the underlying job is defending numbers in front of management, and the pain of having « no answer » for the director weighs more than the error itself. > "If I know the data is from last night, I can explain it." > - Claire Martin, [[interview-claire-martin]] ## Connections - underlies [[users-want-to-see-where-each-number-comes-from-and-when-data]] - provenance matters because it makes numbers explainable

title: Pulse numbers do not always match the carrier's data
body: The participant states that Pulse figures diverge from the carrier's figures, with a concrete example: a delay rate shown as 4% that was actually 7%. A discrepancy of this size on a headline metric undermines the tool's value as a reporting source. > "Because the numbers in Pulse don't always match the carrier's. Last time, I presented a 4% delay rate when it was actually 7%." > - Claire Martin, [[interview-claire-martin]]

title: The numbers are trusted as accurate
body: The participant, who cross-checks Pulse data in his own warehouse, says he has never seen a discrepancy in the numbers. Stated once, but from a well-placed observer. It suggests trust issues with Pulse lie in meaning and definitions rather than data accuracy. > "The numbers are right, on my side I've never seen a discrepancy." > - Karim Benali, [[interview-karim-benali]]

title: Unclear metric definitions lead each team to interpret them its own way
body: Metric definitions are not documented anywhere, so teams interpret them differently. The participant gives a concrete example: whether a *delay* is measured against the promised slot or the estimated time. Inconsistent interpretations can lead teams to different conclusions from the same dashboard. > "But the definitions aren't clear. A "delay", is that relative to the promised slot or to the estimated time? It's not written anywhere. So each team interprets it its own way." > - Karim Benali, [[interview-karim-benali]] ## Connections - contextualizes [[the-numbers-are-trusted-as-accurate]] - the trust gap is about meaning, not accuracy

title: Users want a glossary of metrics inside the tool
body: Alongside the API, the participant asks for a glossary of metric definitions directly within Pulse. Stated once, as a secondary item in his time-saving answer. It directly addresses the inconsistent interpretation of metrics across teams. > "And a glossary of the metrics right inside the tool." > - Karim Benali, [[interview-karim-benali]] ## Connections - extends [[unclear-metric-definitions-lead-each-team-to-interpret-them]] - the requested fix for that problem

title: Users want to see where each number comes from and when data was last synced
body: Asked what would help, the participant asks for data provenance: a link to the source of each number or the date of the last sync. The request is stated once, in answer to a direct question, and is modest in scope - visibility rather than a new feature set. > "Honestly, seeing where each number comes from. Just a link to the source, or the date of the last sync." > - Claire Martin, [[interview-claire-martin]] ## Connections - addresses [[after-a-wrong-figure-reached-management-numbers-are-no]] - provenance is the proposed remedy for the loss of trust
